context: The queuing mutex synchronization pattern places a thread into a wait queue when attempting to lock an already-locked mutex, and on unlock with waiting threads, passes the lock directly to a waiting thread while leaving the mutex in the locked state.

(not provided) ### **4.4 Other Synchronization Patterns** Recall that synchronization refers to any form of control over the relative timing of two or more threads. As such, synchronization includes more than just mutual exclusion; a programmer may want to impose some restriction on relative timing other than the rule of one thread at a time. In this section, I present three other patterns of synchronization that crop up over and over again in many applications: bounded buffers, readers/writers locks, and barriers.
